query: Which focal biodiversity indicators and survey methods (transects, camera traps, species surveys), sampling frequency, and power are needed to detect ecological change and link to social outcomes?

response.query: Which focal biodiversity indicators and survey methods (transects, camera traps, species surveys), sampling frequency, and power are needed to detect ecological change and link to social outcomes?
response.answer: Camera traps are highly effective for detecting ecological change, while transects and species surveys are useful. Frequent sampling and high power are needed to link ecological changes to social outcomes.

results.title: Spatially Explicit Capture-Recapture Through Camera ...
results.content: Finally, the ease of setup and relatively low maintenance requirements for camera traps allows researchers to establish a higher density of traps within their camera array compared to more traditional methods, with more than one trap within the average home range size of the species studied, another requirement of SECR analysis (Borchers and Efford, 2008; Royle et al., 2009, 2018). SECR density estimation through camera trapping is currently focused on rare, elusive, large-ranging, and individually identifiable carnivores, specifically large felids, and this methodology represents one of the best ways to study these species. In order to increase the efficacy of SECR density estimation through camera trapping, especially in the context of long-term population monitoring, researchers must adopt new techniques and technologies e.g., automatic detection through artificial intelligence ([Norouzzadeh et al., 2018), online data entry and verification platforms (eMammal:: )] to increase the scale of their investigations and improve the precision of density estimates.
